Traditional Mead

Served at: Noaptea Lupilor

About 1 gallon (3.8 liters)Prep 15 minCook 4 to 6 weeks fermentation

Mead is a fermented honey wine that has been enjoyed for centuries, often associated with ancient rituals and celebrations. During Noaptea Lupilor, or the Night of the Wolves, mead is traditionally served to honor the mystical connection between humans and nature, symbolizing strength and unity.

Ingredients

  • 3 lbs (1.36 kg) honey
  • 1 gallon (3.8 L) spring water
  • 1 packet wine yeast (such as Lalvin D-47 or EC-1118)
  • 1 tsp yeast nutrient
  • Optional: 1 cinnamon stick or a few cloves for flavor

Method

  1. Sterilize all equipment thoroughly to prevent contamination.
  2. Warm half of the water to about 110°F (43°C) and dissolve the honey into it, stirring well.
  3. Pour the honey-water mixture into a sanitized fermentation vessel and add the remaining water to bring the total volume to 1 gallon.
  4. Allow the mixture to cool to room temperature if it has warmed too much.
  5. Add the yeast nutrient and stir gently.
  6. Pitch the yeast by sprinkling it on top of the must (the honey-water mixture).
  7. Cover the vessel with an airlock or a clean cloth secured with a rubber band to allow gases to escape while preventing contaminants.
  8. Place the fermenter in a dark, cool area (around 65-75°F or 18-24°C) and let it ferment for 4 to 6 weeks, or until bubbling stops.
  9. After fermentation, siphon the mead into a clean container, leaving sediment behind.
  10. Optionally, add spices like cinnamon or cloves at this stage for additional flavor and let it age for another 1-2 weeks.
  11. Bottle the mead in sterilized bottles and seal tightly.
  12. Allow the mead to age for at least 3 months for best flavor before serving.

Tips

  • Use high-quality honey for the best flavor and aroma.
  • Maintain a consistent fermentation temperature to ensure proper yeast activity.
  • Be patient with aging; mead improves significantly with time and will develop smoother, richer flavors.
